You are doing an EXHAUSTIVE, authoritative research pass on Confluence for the Zimmermann SFCC/PWA project. Your single goal: find everything Confluence says about UNIT TEST COVERAGE for the PWA (Progressive Web App / storefront frontend) repository — targets, thresholds, policies, QA process, and any statement about whether a coverage % gate exists.

IMPORTANT — the Atlassian MCP tools are DEFERRED. You MUST load their schemas first, in ONE call:
ToolSearch with query: select:mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_search,mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_page,mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_space_page_tree,mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_page_children,mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_comments

Context:
- Confluence base URL: https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki
- Primary space key: SFCC
- This is a Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SFCC) program. There are TWO codebases: (a) the PWA Kit FRONTEND storefront repo (React/TypeScript, Vitest/Storybook/Playwright), and (b) a separate SFCC BACKEND cartridge repo. A ~90% code-coverage requirement is believed to apply ONLY to the backend cartridge repo, NOT the PWA frontend. Your job is to VERIFY this precisely and find any coverage numbers, being explicit about WHICH repo each number applies to.

Method — be deep and exhaustive, do not stop at the first hit:
1. Run MANY confluence_search CQL queries. Vary terms: "unit test coverage", "test coverage", "code coverage", "coverage threshold", "coverage target", "coverage gate", "Vitest", "unit test", "unit testing", "Jest", "testing strategy", "test strategy", "QA process", "quality gate", "definition of done", "DoD", "acceptance criteria testing", "CI pipeline", "qa.yml", "Storybook", "Playwright", "E2E", "Istanbul", "nyc", "coverage report", "SonarQube", "code quality".
2. Pull the SFCC space page tree (confluence_get_space_page_tree) and scan every page title for testing/QA/quality/standards/coverage pages. Follow children of any Testing/QA/Standards/Architecture/Setup parent pages.
3. Open every promising page FULLY (confluence_get_page with body). Quote exact coverage numbers, requirements, and policy statements verbatim.
4. Check page comments on key pages if relevant.

Report back a verbose, well-structured findings document containing:
1. Every relevant page: exact title, page ID, full URL, and last-updated date.
2. Every coverage number/target found, each explicitly labelled with WHICH repo/codebase it applies to (PWA frontend vs SFCC backend cartridge vs ambiguous).
3. A clear verdict on: "Does Confluence define a unit-test coverage % threshold for the PWA frontend repo?" (yes/no + evidence).
4. Any testing-strategy, QA-process, or definition-of-done docs relevant to PWA unit tests.
5. Direct verbatim quotes for every key claim, each with page-title + ID attribution.
6. A list of the exact CQL queries you ran and how many results each returned, so the search is auditable.

Do not make code changes. Do not edit any Confluence page. Read-only. Be thorough and verbose — this is an authoritative audit that will be quoted.
